editorial:
Ever wonder why giving birth feels more like a medical procedure than a natural event? You will get some eye-opening answers here. Filmmaker Abby Epstein and producer Ricki Lake team up to dive deep into the world of modern maternity care. It feels like a friendly but honest conversation about how we handle pregnancy today. The vibe is curious and a bit rebellious, as they question why certain hospital rules exist and look at different ways people choose to bring babies into the world. It is not just about medical facts; it is about the human experience of becoming a parent.

What really works here is the variety of stories, including some surprising celebrity birth tales that make the heavy topics feel lighter. The pacing is steady, though some parts feel more like an educational class than a movie. If you are expecting a fast-paced thriller, this isn't it, but for anyone wanting to feel more empowered about health choices, it is gold. You can grab this as a DVD set to keep in your physical collection or look for it on digital rental platforms. It is a great pick for expecting parents or anyone who likes documentaries that challenge the status quo.
endingExplained: The series wraps up by encouraging you to take charge of your own birth plan. Instead of just following the crowd, it shows that you have the right to ask questions and choose your environment. The final scenes summarize the main goal: moving away from a one-size-fits-all medical approach. It ends on a hopeful note, leaving you feeling like you have the tools to make safer and more personal choices for your future family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves learning about health and wellness or is preparing for a baby.
